newsitem.title: USA: Centennial Tech faces shareholder lawsuits.
newsitem.headline: Centennial Tech faces shareholder lawsuits.

text.p: The law firm Berman DeValerio & Pease LLP said on Wednesday it filed suit in U.S. District Court in Massachusetts, to recover damages on behalf of all persons who purchased common stock of Centennial Technologies Inc from August 21 through February 10, 1997.

The complaint charges Centennial and certain of its officers with violations of sections of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 arising from the company's February 11 announcement that its financial results were materially overstated during parts of its fiscal years 1996 and 1997.
Separately, lawyers in at Wolf Popper LLP and Shapiro, Haber & Urmy LLP said on Wednesday that they have also filed suit against the company on substantially similar grounds.
Centennial representatives were not immediately available for comment on the latest in a number of lawsuits filed on behalf of purchasers of its stock.
Centennial's former chief executive, Emanual Pinez, faces federal charges including insider trading, overstating revenue and manipulating inventory.

The company, which boasted the best-performing share price of 1996 on the New York Stock Eschange, said on Tuesday it would restate its results to show losses for 1996 and the first quarter of 1997, as well as revising its second-quarter 1997 results to show a loss.
In a statement on Tuesday, the company said "Certain financial records of the company appear to have been falsified and may affect the ability to determine the accuracy of financial statements."
Centennial shares were trading at 2-1/4 Wednesday afternoon, down 5/8 from Tuesday's close, a session in which shares dropped 75 percent from their last trade eight days earlier.
